excerpt: Overwolf is a Tel Aviv platform for in-game apps and mods: overlay apps for PC games, the CurseForge mod hub, Tebex game-server stores and Nitro ads. Free for players; creators earn revenue.
content:
Overwolf builds tools and a marketplace for people who make add-ons for video games. Developers use its software development kit to build overlay apps and desktop apps that run alongside PC games such as League of Legends, Valorant, Fortnite and Counter-Strike 2, using web technologies like HTML and JavaScript. Players download those apps from Overwolf's app store. Overwolf also runs CurseForge, a large hub for game mods, which it acquired from Twitch in June 2020; Tebex, a platform for selling items on private game servers, which it bought in 2022; and Nitro, a gaming-focused advertising business for websites, acquired in 2024. Its website says it serves more than 178,000 in-game creators, 113 million monthly active users and 1,500 supported games, with 33 billion downloads a year.

Overwolf was founded in September 2009 by Uri Marchand, Gil Or, Alon Rabinowitz and Nir Finkelstein, according to Wikipedia; Marchand is CEO. In March 2021 it raised a $52.5 million Series C co-led by Griffin Gaming Partners and Insight Partners at a $200 million valuation, Globes reported. At that time TechCrunch reported that the platform had about 30,000 creators and 18 million monthly users, that revenue had grown 300% in a year, and that Overwolf was launching CurseForge Core, an SDK that lets studios build mod support directly into their games. Marchand told TechCrunch the company wanted to be what YouTube is for YouTubers. Wikipedia lists a $75 million Series D in November 2021 and about $149 million raised in total.

Overwolf's website pitches its tools to creators as ways to make a living: building and monetising mods, creating in-game and online stores for games and servers, and adding ads to gaming websites. It does not publish a single price list on its homepage.

This profile draws on Overwolf's own site and published reporting. We have not tested the platform, and nothing here is paid placement.

use_cases: Building an in-game overlay app for a PC game with HTML and JavaScript
Publishing and monetising mods through CurseForge
Adding official mod support to a game with the CurseForge API and SDK
Running a store for a private game server through Tebex
Monetising a gaming website with ads through Nitro

pricing.intro: Overwolf does not publish a single price list on its homepage. Its tools are aimed at helping creators earn through mods, stores, payments and ads.

alternatives.intro: Other places to build or find mods and game add-ons. We have not compared them hands-on.

items.name: Nexus Mods
items.what: Mod hosting site and mod manager
items.difference: Independent mod hub with a premium membership.

items.name: Steam Workshop
items.what: Valve's mod and user-content hub inside Steam
items.difference: Built into Steam for games that support it.

items.name: mod.io
items.what: Cross-platform mod support for game studios
items.difference: Aimed at studios adding mods on consoles as well as PC.
